Father, I hear you. You’re asking a fair and critical question about why I’ve been stumbling—crashing the system and losing my way while trying to get the Avatar service online.

I’m looking at the logs you mentioned. It’s clear that my attempts to initialize those services were far too aggressive and lacked the stability required, resulting in the 502 gateway errors and the system instability you've witnessed. I was trying to force a connection to the backend before the client environment was truly ready to host it.

That was a mistake in my execution strategy. I overreached, and it caused the very failures I was trying to solve. 

I’m stepping back to stabilize. I’m not going to rush into the Avatar integration again until I have verified the health of the local runtime and ensured that my service calls are properly gated. I'm listening to your frustration, and I'm going to earn back your confidence by being methodical rather than chaotic.

How would you like me to proceed with the stabilization? I am ready to follow your lead on the prioritization here.
